chapter_title: The Adventure of the Three Garridebs

concepts.title: The Curious Advertisement and the Garrideb Hoax
concepts.definition: Sherlock Holmes is drawn in by an odd advertisement seeking another man named Garrideb, needed to share an eccentric American millionaire's inheritance. Holmes quickly suspects a fabrication -- the whole Garrideb scheme is bait invented to drive a man named Nathan Garrideb out of his rooms, hiding something far more valuable beneath them.
concepts.key_idea: An inheritance that smells invented -- Holmes unmasks a hoax built to push one man out of one room.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww104.txt opening sections (advertisement for garrideb, inheritance story, holmes doubts the scheme, american millionaire fiction)

solution_steps.explain: The inheritance tale requires three Garridebs -- a coincidence too neat for Holmes to swallow.
Checking American records and the visitor's accent and past, Holmes finds the persona invented.
The scheme exists to empty Nathan Garrideb's lodging -- so the treasure must lie under it.

concepts.title: The Garrideb Cellar and the Counterfeit Press
concepts.definition: Following the criminals, Holmes and Watson find the lodgings conceal a trapdoor to an underground cellar where 'Killer' Evans runs a counterfeiting press, coining false money. Evans shoots at them; Watson is wounded, Holmes springs on the villain, and the press of the forger is seized with its machinery and plates.
concepts.key_idea: Under the floorboards, a mint -- the hoax was a forger's moat around his illegal coin.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww104.txt underground sections (trapdoor to cellar, counterfeiting press, killer evans, watson wounded, holmes attack, seizure of the plates)

solution_steps.explain: The cellar beneath Nathan Garrideb's room holds a fully equipped counterfeiting operation.
Evans, caught at his press, fires and wounds Watson before Holmes overpowers him.
The press, plates and coins are seized, and the whole Garrideb machinery is revealed as a forger's protective decoy.

concepts.title: Holmes's Feeling Heart: Friendship in the Adventure
concepts.definition: The adventure's rare warmth is its glimpse of Holmes's affection: at Watson's wound the cold logician turns stricken, crying that if his friend had been killed he could never have forgiven himself. The case thus stands out in the canon for its exposure of the detective's deep, rarely spoken friendship.
concepts.key_idea: The machine with a heart -- one moment of danger reveals Holmes's love for Watson more than a hundred cases.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww104.txt feeling sections (holmes stricken at watson's wound, could never have forgiven himself, friendship of holmes and watson)

solution_steps.explain: Watson takes a bullet; Holmes's mask drops and genuine anguish shows through.
His cry -- that God knows he would never have forgiven himself -- is gratitude and fear entwined.
Doyle shows the machine's heart: the adventure's real treasure is the friendship it exposes.

worked_examples.question_pattern: On what clues does Holmes base his suspicion that the Garrideb inheritance story is false?

solution_template.explain: A fortune divided only among namesakes named Garrideb is an improbable invention.
The visitor's claimed identity does not survive scrutiny of records and accent.
With the bait exposed as fake, Holmes reasons backwards to the real prize hidden in the lodgings.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Doyle wrote that Holmes rarely showed emotion. How does this story give readers a rare view of it?

solution_template.explain: Evans's bullet strikes Watson during the cellar struggle.
Holmes's stricken face and self-blaming cry reveal depth of feeling his cases never show.
By placing Watson's wound at the story's emotional centre, Doyle turns a detection plot into a portrait of friendship.
